headline: Sensorimotor alignment correlates with embodied-model success in limited cohorts
summary: A new preprint introduces Sensorimotor Alignment (S²), a training-free offline metric comparing a model’s sensory-feature neighborhoods with recorded robot-motion neighborhoods. The authors report that S² correlates with task success across 12 vision-language-action models (Pearson r=0.717; model-bootstrap 95% CI 0.436–0.912), as well as smaller VLM and world-action-model cohorts. The result suggests a possible low-cost screening signal before closed-loop evaluation, but it is correlational, tested on few model families, and does not show that optimizing S² improves success. The authors’ code guide also says their highlighted real-robot correlation uses an exploratory horizon; at the paper-prespecified horizon it is weaker.
